team.bio_html:
Drake Filippis is an Associate Broker with Signature Associates and founder of Midwest Industrial Brokers (midwestindustrialbrokers.com), his dedicated platform focused on his specialization in industrial real estate, with deep experience in manufacturing, cold storage, heavy power, R&D, flex, multi-tenant, and R&D lab space, as well as large distribution and big-box sale and lease transactions.

Raised in a Midwest industrial town and educated at Purdue University alongside top industrial, mechanical, and robotics engineers, Drake built an early fluency in how manufacturers and logistics operators actually use buildings, further sharpening his focus where industrial infrastructure and technology meet.

At Signature Associates, Drake has been mentored directly by the highest-producing industrial brokers in the Midwest, where industrialization has dominated for over a century, because things have always been built in Detroit. He works closely with state, county, municipal, and economic development agencies to navigate site selection, workforce incentives, and municipal approvals for economically stimulating businesses.

services.description: Freezer, cooler, tri-temp (-20°F to 55°F) and USDA/FDA food-grade warehouse brokerage and build-to-suit across Michigan, Ohio and the Midwest cold chain.
services.headline: Michigan, Ohio and Midwest cold storage, freezer/cooler and food logistics real estate
services.meta: Cold storage, freezer, cooler and USDA/FDA food-grade industrial real estate across Michigan, Ohio and the Midwest. Tri-temp (-20°F to 55°F), blast freezing, ammonia/CO2/freon refrigeration and build-to-suit along I-75, I-94 and I-80/I-90. Call Drake Filippis at (248) 941-1125.
overview: Cold storage is one of the most specialized and supply-constrained segments in Midwest industrial real estate. Food processors, cold chain 3PLs, grocery distributors, pharmaceutical operators and agricultural exporters cannot simply move into a standard dry warehouse. They need verified refrigeration tonnage, insulated metal panel (IMP) envelopes, under-slab glycol or electric floor heat to prevent frost heave, vapor barriers, sealed refrigerated dock aprons and strict USDA, FDA, SQF or BRC compliance.

Midwest Industrial Brokers serves as a dedicated Michigan, Ohio and Midwest hub for cold storage acquisitions, leasing, dispositions and cold build-to-suit development. Along the primary Great Lakes cold chain corridors connecting Metro Detroit (Taylor, Romulus, Detroit Metro Airport and I-94/I-75), Western Michigan, and Northwest Ohio (Toledo, Rossford and Swanton at the I-75 and I-80/I-90 Ohio Turnpike crossroads), Drake Filippis helps cold chain operators secure existing freezer/cooler facilities or deliver purpose-built cold storage on schedule.

Whether your operation requires -20°F deep-freeze storage, 0°F freezer bays, 34°F to 38°F perishable cooler rooms, 55°F climate-controlled food packaging areas, blast freezing cells, or dry warehouse space with structural capacity and power to convert into cold storage, Drake evaluates every technical detail before you commit.

faqs.q: Where are the primary cold storage corridors in Michigan and Ohio?
faqs.a: The strongest cold chain hubs sit along I-94 and I-75 near Detroit Metro Airport (Taylor and Romulus, MI) and at the junction of I-75 and the I-80/I-90 Ohio Turnpike in Northwest Ohio (Rossford, Swanton and Toledo, OH). These locations reach over 50% of North American consumers and Canadian border crossings within a one-day truck drive.

faqs.q: Do you have active cold storage listings in Michigan and Ohio?
faqs.a: Yes. Active opportunities include large-scale freezer/cooler and build-to-suit cold storage facilities such as DTW Taylor Cold Storage (up to 249,700 SF in Taylor, MI), DTW Romulus Cold Storage (258,000 SF in Romulus, MI), Rossford Cold Storage (up to 258,000 SF in Rossford, OH), and Land Air Cold Storage (up to 258,700 SF in Swanton, OH), alongside off-market freezer/cooler buildings.

faqs.q: What should a food or cold storage user check before leasing or buying a building?
faqs.a: Critical items include under-slab heating (glycol loops or electric heat trace) to prevent sub-freezing frost heave, insulation R-values and vapor barrier integrity, compressor and condenser age and refrigerant type (ammonia vs. freon/CO2), primary 480V power capacity, refrigerated dock seals and levelers, floor drains and municipal water/sewer pretreatment capacity.

overview: The reindustrialization of the American Midwest and the reshoring of critical manufacturing supply chains have created intense demand for existing industrial buildings with heavy electrical infrastructure. Today, power availability and utility upgrade timelines are often the single biggest bottleneck in industrial site selection.

Many marketing flyers list 'heavy power' without verifying whether the switchgear, pad-mounted transformers, primary utility feeders or nearby substations actually have the available KVA/MVA capacity to run the buyer's machinery. Drake Filippis goes beyond the listing sheet to verify true primary and secondary voltage (480V/277V 3-phase, 2,000A to 10,000A+ bus-duct distribution, 13.2kV or 40kV primary service, and on-site KVA transformer ratings).

When a building or greenfield site needs a service upgrade, Drake connects clients with trusted industrial electrical engineers and works directly alongside DTE Energy, Consumers Energy and municipal electric utilities to evaluate feeder capacity, transformer lead times, load factors and utility infrastructure incentives before you sign a lease or purchase agreement.

faqs.q: How do you verify if an industrial building truly has the power capacity advertised?
faqs.a: We inspect the physical electrical room and transformer pad to check main switchgear ratings, voltage (208V/240V vs. 480V 3-phase), KVA nameplate ratings on transformers, and whether the service is primary or secondary metered. We then verify with DTE Energy or Consumers Energy that the local circuit and substation can support your connected and peak demand load.

faqs.q: Can you help increase power capacity at an existing building?
faqs.a: Yes. Through our network of industrial electrical contractors and contacts at DTE Energy, Consumers Energy and local municipalities, we help buyers and tenants scope transformer upgrades, new primary feeds, switchgear replacements and utility cost-sharing programs based on your load factor and job creation.

faqs.q: Why are companies choosing Southeast Michigan for onshoring and reindustrialization?
faqs.a: Southeast Michigan has one of the deepest inventories of heavy-power, crane-served manufacturing buildings in North America, backed by a skilled industrial workforce, tool-and-die ecosystem, international border crossings to Canada, and aggressive state and local reindustrialization incentives.

Positioned between the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, the I-275 technology corridor (Plymouth, Livonia, Canton, Novi, Wixom), and the I-75 automation alley in Oakland and Macomb counties (Auburn Hills, Troy, Rochester Hills, Sterling Heights, Warren), the region houses the highest concentration of robotics integrators, machine vision firms and industrial engineering talent in the country.

Robotics and automation facilities require a specific hybrid footprint: high-image engineering and software offices up front paired with high-bay assembly, integration and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) bays in the rear. Those production bays demand unobstructed column spacing, reinforced flat concrete slabs for AGVs and precision alignment, overhead bridge cranes, clean regulated 480V power, compressed air lines and oversized grade-level or dock doors to ship completed automation cells.

Drake Filippis represents robotics startups, global automation tier-1s, custom machine builders and precision manufacturers in securing headquarters, integration facilities and R&D centers across Michigan and the broader Midwest engineering belt.

overview: In a legacy manufacturing state like Michigan, many of the best-located industrial buildings and infill land sites, complete with heavy power, rail spurs and interstate frontage, carry some history of prior industrial use. Buyers from outside Michigan often walk away from great buildings because they do not understand Michigan's unique statutory liability protection: the Baseline Environmental Assessment (BEA).

Under Part 201 of Michigan's Natural Resources and Environmental Protection Act (NREPA), overseen by EGLE, a new buyer or tenant who conducts a Phase I/Phase II environmental assessment and timely submits a Baseline Environmental Assessment (BEA) within the statutory window can acquire a contaminated industrial property without becoming liable for pre-existing contamination, provided they exercise 'Due Care' for safe occupancy.

Beyond environmental protection, Drake Filippis works directly with municipal, county and state economic development professionals, including the Michigan Economic Development Corporation (MEDC), Oakland County, Wayne County, Washtenaw County, Macomb County and local township supervisors, to help job-creating industrial companies access Brownfield TIF reimbursement, PA 198 industrial property tax abatements, workforce training grants and utility infrastructure support.

faqs.q: What is a Michigan Baseline Environmental Assessment (BEA) and why is it so important for industrial buyers?
faqs.a: Michigan is one of the few states where a new buyer or tenant of a contaminated property can obtain statutory protection from cleanup liability for existing contamination. By completing a Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessment prior to or within 45 days after acquisition and filing a BEA with EGLE within 6 months, the buyer is protected from liability for pre-existing conditions and only needs to comply with 'Due Care' obligations to keep occupants safe.

faqs.q: When should a company contact economic development agencies about incentives?

faqs.q: How does Drake help owners sell or lease an industrial building?
faqs.a: Disposition starts with a walkthrough and a review of the building, the market and your goals. From there Drake builds a pricing and marketing plan, lists the property on CPIX and other industrial channels, reaches out to likely buyers or tenants, and manages tours, offers, negotiation and due diligence through closing or lease signing.

faqs.q: How does an acquisition search work for owner users and investors?
faqs.a: It begins with a clear list of requirements, such as size, clear height, power, loading, yard, zoning, location and budget. Drake then searches listed and off market options, sets up tours, helps compare buildings side by side, and negotiates the purchase. He also helps coordinate inspections, environmental review, title and financing timing so the deal can close on schedule.

faqs.q: What is a build-to-suit and when does it make sense?
faqs.a: A build-to-suit is a new facility designed and built around a specific user. It can make sense when no existing building meets your needs, or when your operation needs special features like heavy power, high clear height or extra loading. Drake helps with site selection, entitlements and coordination with developers and contractors, and can compare build-to-suit options with existing buildings.

faqs.q: How long does it take to lease industrial space?
faqs.a: It depends on the size of the space, how many options fit, the condition of the building and how much work is needed before move in. A simple lease of a ready space can move quickly, while larger spaces or spaces that need improvements often take longer. Starting early gives you more choices and more negotiating room, so it is smart to reach out well before your current lease ends.

faqs.q: What should I have ready before I start a search?
faqs.a: Helpful details include the size you need, ceiling height, number and type of loading doors, power, parking and yard needs, preferred areas, budget, and your move in date. If you are buying, it also helps to know your financing plan. Drake can help you work through any of these if you are not sure yet.

faqs.q: Do you represent tenants, buyers, landlords and sellers?
faqs.a: Yes. Drake represents owners on disposition and leasing, and represents buyers and tenants on acquisitions and leases. On every assignment the representation is confirmed in writing at the start so everyone knows who is represented.

faqs.q: Which areas do you cover?
faqs.a: Drake focuses on industrial property in Plymouth, Livonia, Canton, Ann Arbor, Saline, Novi, Northville, Wixom, the I-275 corridor and greater Metro Detroit. Through Signature Associates he also handles assignments in other parts of Michigan and the region.
